Selected work

Learning products built for real constraints.

These systems connect standards, student agency, technical rigor, assessment, and stakeholder review—then make the work usable by other educators.

01

Curriculum system · Engineering Design

EDP I & II: a year-long path from problem framing to flight-ready evidence

Designed an integrated sequence that turns NASA HUNCH review gates into teachable milestones. Students move through research, requirements, CAD, prototyping, testing, documentation, and formal design reviews while maintaining clear evidence of growth.

Audience
High-school engineering students and partner teachers
Product decisions
Scaffolded units, mixed-experience teams, visible review gates, reusable teacher guidance
Evidence
Six national-finalist teams and a district-scale PDR/CDR review process
View the curriculum system ↗
02

Program design · Robotics

Robotics Generational Program

A 26-session progression that develops subsystem competence, integration discipline, evidence-based readiness, and reliable team handoffs—so knowledge compounds across student cohorts.

  • 13 competencies
  • 8 subsystems
  • 12 readiness criteria
Explore the roadmap ↗
03

Learning tool · Assessment

Interactive Competency Tracker

A browser-based tool that makes skill expectations and evidence visible. Learners can track progression across a four-level scale while retaining data locally—supporting reflection without introducing unnecessary infrastructure.

  • Evidence-centered
  • Local storage
  • JSON portability
Open the tracker ↗
04

Systems learning · NASA HUNCH

Rover fleet: authentic engineering as the curriculum spine

Students work across mechanical, electrical, autonomy, navigation, communications, and mission-operations subsystems. The learning architecture uses real interfaces and review criteria to teach decomposition, collaboration, testing, and technical communication.

Subsystem skills→Interface tests→Integrated mission

How I lead curriculum

Discovery, design, pilots, evidence.

  1. 01

    Find the real need

    Translate standards, user needs, technical constraints, and stakeholder goals into a clear learning problem.

  2. 02

    Build the roadmap

    Sequence concepts, practice, formative checks, projects, and teacher supports around visible outcomes.

  3. 03

    Pilot in context

    Teach and test with real learners, then equip colleagues to deliver the experience with confidence.

  4. 04

    Review and improve

    Use artifacts, demonstrations, milestone data, and stakeholder feedback to improve content quality.
